faqs.a:
(a)
Any site assessment provided for under this article shall be performed by qualified
               and trained personnel who shall adhere to the most stringent scientific methods, testing
               measures, procedures and criteria in performing site assessments and evaluating results
               related thereto concerning potentially environmentally contaminated property. A site
               assessment performed by, or at the direction of, an owner shall be subject to review
               by the city for thoroughness, completion, scope, adequacy, clarity and any other factor
               which may be necessary to determine the nature, presence, or extent of hazardous substances
               present in, at, on, over, or under real property that is assessed as provided in this
               article.
(1)
The determination as to whether a site assessment is to be performed, or whether a
               higher phase of assessment is necessary, shall be made by the city manager, or his
               designee after consultation with the employee identified as having responsibility
               for review and analysis of site assessments as described in subsection (b) of this
               section.
(2)
Any determination that a Phase I or higher assessment is necessary shall, at a minimum,
               consider whether a hazardous substance may reasonably be believed to exist in the
               property; the planned or potential use of the property; the potential economic, health,
               or safety consequences of permitting a potentially hazardous waste to remain unidentified
               or unremediated on the property; proximity of the hazardous waste to contaminable
               sources such as groundwater; the proximity of the hazardous waste to adjacent property;
               the potential exposure of the general populace to hazardous substances by incidental
               contact; as well as appropriate standards and requirements established by the Colorado
               Department of Public Health and Environment and the Environmental Protection Agency
               concerning lawful and/or hazardous contaminant levels regarding the nature and make
               up of the property in question. The city may further adopt, in the manner described
               in subsection (d) of this section, such other factors, criteria, standards, requirements,
               or procedures as may be reasonably necessary to implement the provisions of this article.
(3)
The city may reject any assessment which in the reasonable judgment of the city does
               not sufficiently identify the nature and scope of the hazardous material or substances,
               or which otherwise fails to enumerate such necessary activity or actions as may be
               required to remediate the condition of environmental contamination, or which is otherwise
               defective because of inadequacy or faulty performance by the person or company performing
               such assessment. Rejection of an assessment by the city shall not relieve any property
               owner of the responsibility for having an assessment performed as may be required
               under this article.
(b)
The city manager shall designate an employee who, together with such other duties
               as may be assigned, shall be responsible for receiving, reviewing, and analyzing site
               assessment reports, and for providing and planning remediation monitoring activities.
(c)
Notwithstanding any requirement of this article, or any contractual agreement between
               the city and an owner, or any other participation by the city in performing or reviewing
               assessments, the city shall not warrant or guarantee the environmental condition of
               any property to any property owners or third party. When a site assessment has been
               performed by the city or at its direction, such assessment shall be for the exclusive
               use of the city in evaluating the property for the city's purposes. Information obtained
               by the city from a site assessment shall be public information to the extent required
               under applicable state and federal law.
(d)
When any determination required under this article is to be made by the city, and
               has not been otherwise provided for by this article, the city shall promulgate such
               rules and regulations as are necessary and appropriate. The city shall observe the
               administrative rule making procedure in developing such rules and/or regulations.
               The city shall be authorized to establish such regulations and rules as it deems necessary
               and appropriate for the implementation in this article or to otherwise implement the
               rules, regulations, laws, or statutes promulgated by the Colorado Department of Public
               Health and Environment or the Environmental Protection Agency.
(Code 1981, § 25-87; Ord. No. 3009, § 1, 10-4-1993)
